questions.q: Two charged particles, having same kinetic energy, are allowed to pass through a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the direction of motion. If the ratio of radii of their circular paths is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and their respective masses ratio is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Then, the ratio of their charges will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Radius of charged particle moving in circular path R=2mKqB, here, B is magnetic field and K is kinetic energy.

So, q=2mKRB

Now, ratio of the charges is q1q2=m1 m2×R2R1=94×56=54

questions.q: In a co-axial straight cable, the central conductor and the outer conductor carry equal currents in opposite directions. The magnetic field is zero :

questions.solution:
Since the current carried by the outer and inner are equal and in opposite direction, magnetic field produced by the cylinders at a point P(distance r from central axis) is

⇒B→outer=μo4πidl→×r→r3

⇒B→inner=-μo4πidl→×r→r3

⇒B→=B→outer+B→inner=0

The ratio of the magnetic field in first case to that of second case is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As in both cases, length of the wire will remain the same, therefore

l=2πRN=2πrn⇒Rr=nN

Now magnetic field due to single circular coil is given by, B=μ0I2r.

Therefore, required ratio of total magnetic field wil be,

B1B2=Nμ0I2Rnμ0I2r=N2n2

Fiven that E→=Ek^ and B→=12 j^ mT

Kinetic energy=728 eV

questions.solution: Every part (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi><mi>l</mi></math> ) of the wire is pulled by the force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>l</mi><mo>)</mo><mi>B</mi></math> acting perpendicular to the current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>&</mo></math> magnetic field giving it the shape of a circle.

questions.q: A charge particle is moving in a uniform magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. If it has an acceleration of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">α</mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that uniform magnetic field, $\vec{B}=(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}) T$
Acceleration $\vec{a}=(\alpha \hat{i}-4 \hat{j}) \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ We know that
$F=q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) \Rightarrow m \vec{a}=q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$
Here, $\vec{a} \perp \vec{B}$, so, $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{B}=0$
$(\alpha \hat{i}-4 \hat{j})(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j})=0 \Rightarrow 2 \alpha-12=0 \Rightarrow \alpha=6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy of a charge q of mass m in potential is given by,

12mv2=qV

mv=2mqV

Then, the radius of the charge will be,

r=2mqVqB

⇒r∝mq

Hence, the ratio of radius of proton to α-particle,

rprα=14×21=12.

The magnitude of $B$ is _____$\times 10^{-1} \mathrm{~T}$ (given, $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{R}=\frac{\rho \ell}{\mathrm{A}} \Rightarrow \frac{2 \times 10^{-6} \times \ell}{10^{-5}}=1 \Rightarrow \ell=5 \\ & \mathrm{mg}=\mathrm{Bi} \ell\end{aligned}\mathrm{B}=\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{i} \ell}=\frac{5}{2 \times 5}=0.5=5 \times 10^{-1} \mathrm{Tesla}$

questions.q: The ratio of magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying coil of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> to the magnetic field at distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> from the centre of coil on its axis is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>:</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the magnetic field at any axial point situated at a distance x from the centre of a circular current carrying conductor of radius r can be written as

B=μ0Ir22r2+x23/2   ...1

Substitute 0 for x in equation (1) to calculate the magnetic field Bc at the centre of the conductor.

Bc=μ0Ir22r2+023/2= μ0Ir22r3=μ0I2r   ...2

Substitute r for x in equation (1) to calculate the magnetic field Br at the given distance from the centre of the conductor.

Br=μ0Ir22r2+r23/2= μ0Ir242r3=μ0I42r   ...3

Divide equation (2) by equation (3) to calculate the required ratio of the magnetic fields.

BcBr=μ0I2rμ0I42r= 22=8

questions.q: A deuteron and a proton moving with equal kinetic energy enter into to a uniform magnetic field at right angle to the field. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> are the radii of their circular paths respectively, then the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mfrac></math> will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>:</mo><mn>1</mn></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, radius of circular path followed by charged particle under perpendicular magnetic field is given by,

R=mvqB and KE=12mv2

Therefore,

⇒R=2mKEqB  Then, R∝mq

⇒RdRp=mdmp×qpqd=21×11=2:1

Thus, x=2.

questions.q:
A current of 5A exists in a square loop of side $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \mathrm{~m}$. Then the magnitude of the magnetic field $B$ at the centre of the square loop will be $p \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~T}$. where, value of p is _____ .
$\left[\right.$ Take $\left.\mu_0=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{TmA}^{-1}\right]$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Let B be the magnetic field due to single side $\begin{aligned} & \text { then } B=\frac{\mu_0 \mathrm{i}}{4 \pi \mathrm{~d}}\left(\sin \theta_1+\sin \theta_2\right) \\ & =\frac{10^{-7} \times 5 \times 2}{\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=2 \times 10^{-6} \\ & \therefore B_{\text {net }} \text { at centre } O=4 B \\ & =8 \times 10^{-6} \end{aligned}$
